ideas.name: fixed_jaw_offset_block
ideas.description: A printed PLA spacer and face that bolts onto the stock fixed jaw with M3 screws. It carries the fixed contact face 8 mm further outward, still vertical, with the same TPU-skinned grooved pad. Paired with the long_slide, it shifts the whole opening range outward by 8 mm.

ideas.name: fixed_jaw_spacer_shim
ideas.description: A 9 mm printed PLA spacer plate (about 20 x 30 mm, 40% infill) bolted between the gripper body and the fixed jaw with the jaw's existing screw pattern. It moves the fixed jaw's face 9 mm outward along the closing axis. The slide's travel is unchanged, so every object closes at a servo angle 0.2 rad later and the widest opening grows from 88 to about 97 mm between pads. The grasp centre shifts about 4.5 mm toward the fixed jaw, which System 1's side-clearance parameter absorbs.
ideas.test: Add a fixed-jaw offset parameter (0 to 12 mm) to the gripper model that translates the fixed jaw body and its pad outward along the closing axis. Run all groups at 9 mm with the current long_slide (46) and pads.

ideas.name: sector_arc_extension
ideas.description: A printed module-1 tooth arc at 50 mm pitch radius, screwed with four M3 screws over the current 46 mm sector, plus a printed 4 mm spacer that drops the carriage rack to the new centre distance. The finger travels 50 mm per servo radian over the same -0.17 to 1.75 rad, so the pads open to about 95 mm. They stay parallel and the tip does not rise, and the squeeze falls only from 35 N to 32 N.
ideas.test: In the simulator, build the long_slide with sector_radius_mm=50 but keep the current carriage, rods and pads (reach 9, width 20), and charge only the arc and spacer print. Rerun all 21 groups, checking tomato_soup_can and apple, which lost to a rack press at 49.5 when the whole slide was reprinted.

ideas.name: flush_reach_pads
ideas.description: Printed PLA tongues that bolt to the back and side of each stock jaw face, with their contact surface coplanar with the stock face (0 mm stand-out), so they add no thickness to the opening. Each tongue extends 12 mm below the stock fingertip, is 20 mm wide, carries a 2 mm V-groove cut into it, and has a 0.5 mm TPU skin (mu 0.9) inset into a pocket so it does not stand proud. The fingertips open to about 95 mm, against 88 mm with the current pads, and still reach below the top of low objects.
ideas.test: A pads variant in design/fingers.py with a stand-out parameter (pad thickness in front of the face, 0–4 mm) and the TPU skin inset into a pocket. Then re-run pudding_box, sugar_box and mustard_bottle at stand-out 0, plus banana, gelatin_box and tuna_fish_can to check that contact height is kept.

proposals.edit: jaw -> long_slide (sector_radius_mm=50)
proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face (pudding_box, sugar_box, mustard_bottle, tuna_fish_can) and fixed_jaw_missed (rva000_sugar_box): the hinged jaw's fingertip rises as it opens, by +14 to +23 mm at the 74-85 mm openings used, and its face tilts 44-64 deg. So on these low wide objects (34-58 mm tall, tops at +17 to +29 mm) the moving tip lands on the top face and pushes 55-84 deg down instead of squeezing the side. The same tilt causes squeezed_down_out on potted_meat_can: at 57 mm the moving face is 33 deg off, contacting at +43 mm when the top is at +42, and tan 33° = 0.65 is more than the metal's friction of 0.35.
proposals.principle: A finger can only hold a side if its fingertip reaches below the object's top at that opening, and only horizontal, opposed (antipodal) contacts hold without squeezing the object out. A slide keeps the finger from turning or rising at any opening.
proposals.hypothesis: No params move can fix this. The stock revolute jaw's tip rise R(1-cos q) is fixed by its 81 mm radius, and the failing objects need 85-96 mm openings, where the brief gives tip +23 to +35 mm and face 53-64 deg. Pads with pad_angle 45 still leave the face at +14 deg and the tip at +14 mm at 85 mm. Parallelogram link 90 keeps the face parallel but its tip rises +33 mm at 85 mm, and link 50 cannot reach 85 mm at all. Prismatic tops out at 68 mm. long_slide at sector_radius 50 is the only catalogue part that reaches 103 mm with face 0 deg, tip +1 mm and 32 N at every width, which covers mustard's 96 mm plus side clearance. Holding force: 2·0.5·32 = 32 N against the sugar box's 5.0 N, 2·0.4·32 = 26 N against mustard's 4.2 N, and 2·0.35·32 = 22 N against potted meat's 3.6 N, all with large margin for the lift's acceleration. Arm load for the heaviest object (514 g) is 0.41 + 0.77 = 1.18 N·m plus about 60 g more at the wrist, still under the 1.62 N·m stall. Cost: $6.40 (lm3uu x2 at $2.40, steel_rod_3x150 x2 at $4.00), 3 days, 216 machine minutes; all within $40, 7 days and 600 minutes. M3 screws are on hand.
risks: Round rollers (apple, golf_ball, tennis_ball, lemon, plum, strawberry, racquetball, tomato_soup_can): flat parallel faces don't centre a sphere along the depth axis. They should survive because the squeeze rises from 20 to 32 N, contacts now sit exactly at the equator with no up/down push, and the stock faces are flat too and already hold these objects. If any fails, a grooved pad (proposal 2's slot) is the remedy.

Small objects (dice 17 mm, large_marker 19 mm): the slide must close below 17 mm. Its servo range starts at -0.17 rad, as the stock jaw's does, so the fully closed position should be about the same; the parameter refit can lower sector_radius if needed, but anything below about 48 mm loses mustard's 96 mm.
Tomato_soup_can (349 g, friction 0.35): it is held at 20 N now, and 32 N with parallel faces only adds margin.
proposals.result: refused before trial: mechanism law (no interference): the wrist and the pinion share material, a region up to 1.6 x 0.2 x 0.5 mm (jaw at -0.17 rad, wrist rolled -2.74..-2.74 rad); parts may share material only at a bearing seat, within 10 mm of the hinge axis

proposals.mechanism: squeezed_down_out on rva000_potted_meat_can: the moving face is 33 deg off parallel at the 57-63 mm opening and pushes the 370 g metal can down with N sin(a). Bare PLA against metal at 0.35 cannot resist that, since tan 33° = 0.65.
proposals.principle: A tilted contact squeezes the object out unless friction exceeds the tilt. A TPU skin raises friction to 0.9, a pad tilted back by pad_angle makes the face parallel nearer the working opening, and a V-groove centres round objects.
proposals.hypothesis: This is the cheapest fallback: $0, 0 days, 16 machine minutes, using on-hand M2 screws and about 3 g of print. With pad_angle 20, the moving face at about 57 mm should drop from about +33 deg to roughly +15 deg (tan 15° ≈ 0.27), well within TPU's 0.9, so the can should stay held through the lift. It does not fix the wide low objects, because the tip still rises on the hinge. It changes a different slot from proposal 1, so if both are kept-eligible they can be combined: on the slide, the TPU and groove add friction and centre the rolling objects.
risks: Small objects (dice, large_marker, wood_block_cube, flat_screwdriver): a 20 deg pad tilts the moving face bottom-in by up to about -20 deg at 17-35 mm, pushing the object upward. TPU friction of 0.9 is more than tan 20° = 0.36, so they should still hold. The refit can trade pad_angle down toward 10 if one slips.

Wide held objects (apple 75 mm, gelatin_box 73 mm, banana 70 mm): their face tilt falls from about 44 to about 25 deg, which helps, and the 2 mm groove and skin narrow the maximum opening by only a few mm (brief: 92-95 mm vs 99 mm). That leaves margin for the 75 mm apple.

proposals.edit: jaw -> long_slide (sector_radius_mm=48.5); pads (groove_mm=2, lip_mm=0, pad_angle_deg=0, pad_tpu_mm=2, reach_mm=0, width_mm=12)
proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face on the wide, low boxes (pudding 90 mm/38 tall, sugar 92/45, tuna 85/34). The hinged jaw cannot open much wider than these objects: its maximum is 91 mm, and near that opening its tip has risen +28 mm or more (+19 to +22 mm in the failing runs). So the moving pad comes down onto the top face (contact at +17 to +22 mm with a top at +19 to +23, pushing 86-88 deg down), and the fixed jaw often never touches. reg_tuna also slipped, with its moving face pushing 10 deg down on metal (mu 0.35).
proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint is parallel to the fixed face at only one opening, and its tip rises by R(1-cos q). A finger that slides straight along the closing axis neither turns nor rises, so its contacts stay antipodal and below the object's top at every opening.
proposals.hypothesis: Iteration 1's long_slide at sector_radius 50 was refused for interference with the wrist, not for its function: the overlap was only 1.6 x 0.2 x 0.5 mm, at jaw -0.17 rad. Cutting the pitch radius to 48.5 mm pulls the sector's rim in by 1.5 mm, about 7 times the 0.2 mm overlap, so it should clear. Opening: 30 mm gives 58 and 50 mm gives 93, so the opening rises about 1.75 mm per mm of radius and seems to stop near 93; 48.5 mm should still give about 92-93 mm. The tip stays at +2 mm and the squeeze is about 1.62/0.0485 = 33 N. With pad_angle set to 0 the slide face is parallel at every opening; it was -20 deg with the current pads. Pudding: 2*0.5*33 = 33 N of grip against 1.8 N of weight. Tuna: 2*0.35*33 = 23 N against 1.7 N, with the face now flat. Sugar: 92 mm against about 93 mm leaves almost no side clearance, so it is uncertain. Shoulder load: 0.41 + about 0.1 for the slide's mass + 0.77 for sugar = about 1.28 N*m, under the 1.62 stall. No params move fixes this. Pads at pad_angle 45 still give the hinge a +14 deg face and a +14 mm tip at 85 mm, and their 95 mm maximum leaves sugar nearly no clearance. Buy: 2 lm3uu ($2.40) and 2 steel_rod_3x150 ($4.00), $6.40 in all, 3 days, about 216 + 16 machine minutes.
risks: It may still be refused for interference if the overlap is not at the sector's rim. If so, the next step is about 47 mm, at the cost of opening.
foam_brick, cup: the squeeze rises from 20 N to about 33 N. Both are light, with high friction or a rigid shell, so they should still hold, though crushing is possible.

Spheres (golf_ball, plum, strawberry, lemon, racquetball, tennis_ball, apple): flat parallel faces leave nothing but the 2 mm groove to centre them. The groove is kept, and parallel faces at the equator are the antipodal ideal, so they should hold better than on the hinge.
dice, large_marker, wood_block_cube: the slide's closed end at -0.17 rad has to come below 17 mm. A pitch radius of 48.5 mm gives about 8 mm of overtravel, so these should still be gripped.

iterations.notes:
I sent three proposals, all aimed at the potted meat can. None of them can fix the pudding box, sugar box or mustard bottle.

**Why the three wide objects stay blocked.** The pudding box (90 mm), sugar box (92 mm) and mustard bottle (96 mm) are wider than the current 88 mm maximum opening. That is why one jaw misses and the other lands on the top face. Nothing in the catalogue can widen the opening right now:
- **A larger gear sector on the slide:** reprinting it takes about 43 g of PLA, roughly 215 machine minutes, and only 98 are left. The record also shows sectors of 48.5 and 49.5 lost the tomato soup can because the longer rack pressed on its top, and 49.5 also lost the apple. Sector 50 was refused because it collides with the wrist. Even about 95 mm would not fit the 96 mm mustard bottle.
- **Prismatic jaw:** refused because it needs 123 machine minutes.
- **Parallelogram jaw:** the moving fingertip rises 44 mm at an 85 mm opening.
- **Stock hinged jaw:** this was already abandoned because tilted faces lost the banana and the large marker.
- **Removing the pads:** this would give 96 mm but takes away the extension, groove and rubber skin that hold the banana, tomato soup can and the round objects.

The right fix is still the recorded idea, a fixed-jaw offset block. It would shift the opening range outward without lengthening the rack, but it has no builder in the simulator, so I did not re-propose it.

**What the proposals change.** Each one shortens how far the pads extend (now 15 mm) and changes nothing else; the three values are 7, 5 and 9 mm. The trial record ties the potted meat can's failure to that extension: it passed with 0 mm and failed with 11 and 15 mm, each time with a pad landing on the can's top. Each proposal costs $0 and about 18 machine minutes for a pads reprint. The bracket is there because two thresholds are uncertain:
- **Banana:** the slide's rack needs some extension below it to clear the banana's top. I estimate about 4.5 mm or more at sector 46.
- **Potted meat can:** the extension it tolerates is unknown, somewhere between 0 and 11 mm.

If I had money for the wide objects, I would spend it on time rather than parts. More machine minutes would allow a jaw reprint, and the $68 12 V servos are not what limits the opening. The sugar box loads the shoulder to about 0.41 + 0.77 = 1.18 N*m, under its 1.62 N*m stall.

iterations.notes:
I'm only proposing a fix for the potted meat can this round. Nothing within the remaining budget can open the jaw wide enough for the pudding box, sugar box or mustard bottle.

**The wide boxes and bottle.** Their mechanism (fixed_jaw_missed, moving_jaw_on_top_face, force_limit) has one root cause: the brief gives a widest opening of 88 mm, and these objects are 90, 92 and 96 mm across. Here is why each fix is out of reach:
- **Larger sector (`sector_radius_mm`):** this means reprinting the long slide (43 g of PLA, about 215 machine minutes; iteration 4 cost 256). Only 83 minutes are left.
- **Prismatic jaw:** refused, 123 minutes.
- **12 V servos:** refused, $68 against $33.60 left, and they don't change the opening anyway.
- **Parallelogram, link 90:** opens to 98 mm, but the fingertip rises +44 mm at 85 mm. That would lose tuna_fish_can, which is 34 mm tall.
- **Stock revolute jaw:** opens to 100 mm, but the face tilts +54 deg at 85 mm, which would push objects out.
- **Removing the pads:** gives 96 mm, but drops the reach and grooves. Reach 0 has lost banana twice, and the eight rolling objects rely on the groove.
- **No TPU skin:** adds only about 2 mm (to roughly 90 mm). That gives the 90 mm pudding box no side clearance, so I don't expect it to gain anything.

The fixed_jaw_offset_block idea from iteration 2 (68 minutes, $0) still fits the budget. Building and testing it is the real route to these three objects, so I haven't re-proposed it.

**The potted meat can.** The two proposals bracket pad width at 21 and 20 mm. I expect them to help the potted meat can, which slips by pivoting at its rim, not from lack of squeeze. Banana is the risk to watch, because width 24 lost it. If neither width works, the can's real limit is grasp depth: the rack sitting above the fingers against the 7 mm reach. Pads can't fix that on this jaw.

idea.description: A 9 mm printed PLA spacer plate (about 20 x 30 mm, 40% infill) bolted between the gripper body and the fixed jaw with the jaw's existing screw pattern. It moves the fixed jaw's face 9 mm outward along the closing axis. The slide's travel is unchanged, so every object closes at a servo angle 0.2 rad later and the widest opening grows from 88 to about 97 mm between pads. The grasp centre shifts about 4.5 mm toward the fixed jaw, which System 1's side-clearance parameter absorbs.
idea.test: Add a fixed-jaw offset parameter (0 to 12 mm) to the gripper model that translates the fixed jaw body and its pad outward along the closing axis. Run all groups at 9 mm with the current long_slide (46) and pads.

- **Proposal 1** removes the TPU skin (a PLA-only reprint, about 10 minutes), which should open the jaw to about 90 mm. It's a long shot: even then the pudding box has almost no clearance, and the sugar box and mustard bottle stay out of reach.
- **Proposal 2** is a new idea, recorded and costed but not tested: pads that sit flush with the jaw face, so they add reach without costing any opening. Expected opening is about 95 mm. It uses only parts on the bench, costs $0 and about 14 machine minutes. It is different from the three earlier ideas, which offset the fixed jaw or extended the gear sector.

The potted meat can hits the force limit at t = 0.02 s, which is too early to be a squeeze. More likely the pads, which now reach 12 mm below the stock fingertips, touch the top of the 84 mm can at the start pose. Shortening reach would put at risk the groups that each 1 mm of reach gained, so I've left it alone this round.

If one more round were affordable, I would buy nothing and spend the machine time reprinting the long slide with sector 50. That opens the jaw to 95 mm at 32 N of squeeze, enough for the pudding and sugar boxes.

proposals.edit: pads (groove_mm=2, lip_mm=0, pad_angle_deg=0, pad_tpu_mm=0, reach_mm=12, width_mm=20)
proposals.mechanism: fixed_jaw_missed / moving_jaw_on_top_face on the wide boxes: the pudding box (90 mm), sugar box (92 mm) and mustard bottle (96 mm) are wider than the jaw opens. The brief gives a maximum fingertip gap of 88 mm at 1.75 rad, the end of the servo range. The jaw closes on air, or the moving pad comes down on the top face (sugar: 5 N at +20 mm, pushing 80 deg down; mustard: 2 N at +17 mm, pushing 58 deg down).
proposals.principle: A finger can only hold an object's side if it opens wider than the object. On a slide, the opening is the sector travel minus the thickness of both pad faces. The brief gives 4 mm per face at pad_tpu_mm=1. Bare faces open to 96 mm, so the pads cost about 8 mm of opening. Removing the 1 mm TPU skin should give back about 2 mm, for an opening of about 90–91 mm.
proposals.hypothesis: Every other way to widen the jaw is refused. A sector of 50 mm needs a long_slide reprint of about 215 min, against the 16 left. The parallelogram needs 82 min and the prismatic 123 min. The 12 V servos cost $68 against $33.60 and would not widen the jaw anyway. pads=none opens to 96 mm, but reach 0 has already put the carriage on 38 mm-tall objects and lost the banana, and the pudding box is also 38 mm tall. The TPU skin is the only part of the face thickness that a pads reprint can change. A reprint with pad_tpu_mm=0 is PLA only: about 10 min, $0, no TPU print time. This keeps reach 12, width 20 and groove 2, which won every held group. It should open the jaw to about 90–91 mm, enough for the 90 mm pudding box with System 1's side clearance near zero (best rva000 run: side=2.8e-05). It will not reach the sugar box (92 mm) or the mustard bottle (96 mm). The cost is friction: 0.45 (bare PLA) instead of 0.9. Even for the 349 g soup can on metal, 2*0.45*35 N = 31.5 N against 3.4 N of weight, so friction still holds about 9x the weight.
risks: tomato_soup_can and tuna_fish_can (metal, 0.35, 349 g and 171 g): the pads' friction drops from 0.9 to 0.45. The plain friction margin is still about 9x, but the soup can lies on its side and rolls, so twist resistance falls too.
golf_ball, tennis_ball, racquetball, apple, lemon, plum, strawberry: round objects that relied partly on high-friction contacts. The 2 mm groove still centres them.
banana: was sensitive to the pad outline. The outline does not change here, only the 1 mm skin, so it should survive.

proposals.mechanism: fixed_jaw_missed on the pudding box (90 mm wide against an 88 mm maximum opening). This is the same opening limit as proposal 1. It adds a hedge against losing the round held objects once friction drops to bare PLA.
proposals.principle: Thinner faces open the jaw wider (opening = travel minus both face thicknesses). A concave or grooved contact centres a round object even when friction alone cannot trap it. A deeper V-groove makes up geometrically for the friction lost with the TPU skin.
proposals.hypothesis: Groove 4 has gained a task and lost none three times: at reach 8, 9 and 10 (iterations 9–11). It lost each time only because a reach step gained more, so it is a known-safe shape change. Pairing it with pad_tpu_mm=0 recovers the opening (about 90–91 mm) and deepens the centring of spheres and rolling cylinders at the lower 0.45 friction. The reprint is PLA only, about 10 min, inside the 16 left. It is tried on its own beside proposal 1, so the trial can tell whether the friction loss needs the groove's help.
risks: tomato_soup_can, tuna_fish_can: lower friction on metal. Groove 4 has held them before, at TPU 1.
banana and flat_screwdriver: a deeper groove changes the contact on long narrow objects. Groove 4 held both at reach 8–10.
dice and large_marker (17 and 19 mm): small objects may sit in a 4 mm groove differently. Groove 4 held them before.
